validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification. Pipeline is real: an existing, actively-progressing 5km/24in gas feeder line supplying the Al-Khalij (Gulf) steam power station in Sirte, built by Sirt Gulf for Gas Projects (SGGP) for client General Electricity Company of Libya (GECOL).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed by two independent origins. (1) alwasat.ly/news/libya/426177 (Libyan news portal, bylined Mahmoud Alsalahi, dated 2024-01-14): 'workers begin implementing the 24[-inch] gas pipeline feeding the Al-Khalij steam power station in Sirte'; names the executing company as 'Khalij Sirte' (Sirt Gulf) Gas Projects Co, says work would take about a week to open the route on the main road. (2) sirtggp.com (the contractor's own site) has a dedicated project page at /projects/supply-and-installation-of-5km-gas-pipeline-24-to-al-khalij-power-plant-sirte/ titled 'Supply and installation of 5km gas pipeline 24" to Al-Khalij power plant (Sirte)', client 'General Electricity Company of Libya', describing 'completion of the first phase ... by cutting the main pipe and installing a Tie-in', dated 2016-02-11. These are two genuinely separate origins (independent news outlet vs. contractor's own site) that both name this exact pipeline, so the sheet's cited sources are not GEM-derived or generic. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is a caveat, not an error — this is a short (5km) lateral/tie-in off an existing trunk to a single power plant rather than a long-haul trunk, but its 24in diameter is transmission-scale and GEM commonly classes such laterals as transmission; not flagging as a concern. DUPLICATE: checked against the roster (P6708, P6715, P6716, P7102, P7617) — no overlap in name, region (Sirte Gulf vs. Mellitah/Sabratha/Bouri in the west, or the proposed Nigeria link), length, or diameter. No duplicate found. Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission already carry a working ref (alwasat) with content present per existing_ref_checks — left as-is.

validity.recommendation: Verify or soften StartLocation=Brega — currently unsupported by any source (sheet's own Location ref_col is MISSING_REF and flagged irregular=true). Consider replacing with the actual tie-in point near Sirte, or leaving Start blank/generic ('Sirte Gulf trunk network') if the tie-in point can't be pinned down.
validity.researcher_notes: The gem.wiki page's own infobox (read for leads only, not cited) carries NO Start/End location detail at all — its 'Location' field just says the pipeline runs 'in Sirte Gulf area, Libya', with no mention of Brega anywhere on the page. That matches the sheet: this Location cluster is MISSING_REF and marked irregular=true, i.e. already an internally-flagged, unsupported field. Independent sources describe this pipeline as a short (5km) feeder that reaches the Al-Khalij plant by 'cutting the main [trunk] pipe and installing a Tie-in' (sirtggp.com) near Sirte itself — not as a line that physically originates ~230km away in Brega town. Web search on the wider Sirte Gulf gas network turned up a separate, much larger project (a new pipeline linking the Farigh field via a 42-inch trunk to Brega and the national grid) that is NOT this pipeline and should not be conflated with it. I found no independent source naming Brega as the specific start point of this 5km/24in segment; 'Brega' looks like a regional inference (Brega is the historic hub of the Gulf-of-Sirte gas/oil network) rather than a verified physical endpoint of this particular lateral. Not fabricating a supporting ref for it.

validity.recommendation: Repoint ProposalYear=2016's ref from alwasat.ly/news/libya/426177 to sirtggp.com's project page — the current ref does not mention 2016 anywhere (confirmed by the sheet's own existing_ref_checks: '200 but data value not found'), while sirtggp.com's dedicated project page for this exact pipeline is dated 2016-02-11 and does support the value.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked both candidate sources directly. alwasat.ly/news/libya/426177 (2024-01-14) is entirely about work starting in January 2024 and never mentions 2016 — the sheet's existing check correctly flagged this as a miss. sirtggp.com's project page for 'Supply and installation of 5km gas pipeline 24" to Al-Khalij power plant (Sirte)' lists 'Date: February 11, 2016' and describes it as completion of the project's first phase (tie-in cut-in), so 2016 is plausibly the right value — it's just cited to the wrong URL in the mainsheet. ConstructionYear=2024 is independently confirmed correct by alwasat's 2024-01-14 article, which describes the main pipe-route work (opening paths on the road) beginning that day. Read together, the timeline is coherent: 2016 tie-in/first-phase work, then a long pause, then the main route implementation resumed in Jan 2024 — not unusual for Libya-era infrastructure. Length=5.00km/Diameter=24in are both independently confirmed (see fills / main validity note).

Was MISSING_REF in the sheet; now filled.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=construction (last GEM update 2025-08-20) is still correct and current. Newest evidence found: GECOL announced 2026-07-20 (reported by alwasat.ly and, separately, by ar.libyaobserver.ly, plus eanlibya.com) that 'preliminary operational tests' at the Al-Khalij gas reception/measurement station succeeded, in preparation for switching the Al-Khalij steam plant's generation units to natural gas; the work is explicitly attributed to 'Sirt Gulf for Gas Projects' (SGGP) — the same contractor named on sirtggp.com's project page for this exact pipeline — under contract to GECOL. eanlibya.com's version explicitly frames this as completing one phase that 'paves the way for the next phases of the project', i.e. the project (and by extension this feeder pipeline) is NOT yet fully commissioned/operating — gas is only in test/commissioning stage at the measurement station, not yet full operations. Combined with alwasat's 2024-01-14 report of main route construction starting, this shows continuous, well-documented progress consistent with 'construction' (now in late-stage commissioning/testing) rather than either stalled or fully operating. Not calling this 'operating' yet since no source states the plant/units are running on gas in production, only that initial tests succeeded and further phases remain. Re-check in the next cycle — given the pace of 2026 announcements this could flip to 'operating' soon.

summary: P6707 (Sirte Gulf PS Gas Pipeline) is real and independently confirmed (contractor's own site + independent Libyan news, 2016–2026): a 5km/24in feeder line tying into the Sirte-area gas trunk to supply the Al-Khalij steam power station, built by SGGP for GECOL. Status=construction confirmed current as of 2026-07 (commissioning/testing phase, not yet operating). Two concerns raised: StartLocation=Brega is unsupported by any source and looks like an unverified regional inference (attribution); ProposalYear=2016's ref is miscited to a page that never mentions 2016 (spec/citation, value itself plausible). Length=5.00km filled with a verified sirtggp.com ref.
